content.text: The cause is the `br` regex in `src/rules.ts:286`. It matches the trailing spaces or backslash and the newline, but nothing consumes the spaces or tabs that start the next line, so they stay in the following text token. The `breaks` variant derives from the same regex (`src/rules.ts:550`), so one change covers both. I'll consume `[ \t]*` after the newline, before the existing lookahead, so a whitespace-only trailing line still doesn't become a break.

content.text:
I fixed the bug in `src/rules.ts`, on the `br` regex at line 286. I haven't run the test suite because the folder has no `node_modules`, so the change is verified by reading the code only. **Cause:** The regex `/^( {2,}|\\)\n(?!\s*$)/` matched the trailing spaces or backslash and the newline, but nothing consumed the spaces or tabs that start the next line. Those stayed in the following text token, so they rendered after the `
`. **Fix:** The regex is now `/^( {2,}|\\)\n[ \t]*(?!\s*$)/`. The `[ \t]*` consumes the continuation line's leading spaces and tabs. The lookahead still follows it, so a break before a whitespace-only line is still not produced. The `breaks` option builds its `br` rule from this same regex (`src/rules.ts:550`), so it gets the same fix. The text rule and the rendered output are unchanged. Expected results: - `foo ⏎ bar` now renders as `

foo
bar

`. - The backslash form `foo\⏎ bar` and tab-indented continuations behave the same way.
